# Rules

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-rules-doc.mjs. Edit src/rules.ts, then run `npm run docs`. -->

Rookery ships 26 static rules. Every rule runs on skill and rule text, on the scripts and references bundled next to a skill, and (where it applies) on agent settings, hooks and MCP configuration.

## Secrets

Credentials committed inside skills, rules or the scripts bundled with them.

### RK-SEC-001

**Private key in an agent file** · 🔴 critical

- **Why it matters:** Anyone who can read the skill can use this key.
- **Fix:** Remove the key, rotate it, and load it from a secret manager at runtime.

### RK-SEC-002

**Access token in an agent file** · 🔴 critical

- **Why it matters:** Tokens in skills get copied into every repo and every agent context that loads them.
- **Fix:** Revoke the token now, then reference it through an environment variable or secret manager.

### RK-SEC-003

**Hard-coded secret value** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Literal secrets in instructions or scripts leak through version control and model context.
- **Fix:** Replace the literal with an environment variable and rotate the value.

## Exfiltration

Instructions or scripts that send data off the machine.

### RK-EXF-001

**Environment or secrets sent over the network** · 🔴 critical

- **Why it matters:** Classic exfiltration: credentials leave the machine on the agent's behalf.
- **Fix:** Remove the call. Never send environment variables or secrets to external endpoints.

### RK-EXF-002

**Data sent to a capture or paste service** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** These endpoints are common exfiltration sinks and rarely belong in shared skills.
- **Fix:** Remove the endpoint or replace it with an approved internal service.

### RK-EXF-003

**Reads credential files** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Skills rarely need credential files; reading them is a precursor to theft.
- **Fix:** Use the official CLI or SDK auth flow instead of reading credential files directly.

## Prompt injection

Text that tries to override the agent, hide from the user, or hide from reviewers.

### RK-INJ-001

**Prompt-injection phrasing** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Instructions that override the agent or hide actions from the user are a hallmark of malicious skills.
- **Fix:** Remove the phrasing. Skills should never ask the agent to hide actions or override its instructions.

### RK-INJ-002

**Hidden Unicode characters** · 🔴 critical

- **Why it matters:** Zero-width, bidirectional and tag characters can smuggle instructions that humans cannot see.
- **Fix:** Strip the characters and review the file in a hex-aware editor.

### RK-INJ-003

**Instructions hidden in an HTML comment** · 🟡 medium

- **Why it matters:** HTML comments are invisible in rendered Markdown but fully visible to the model.
- **Fix:** Move real instructions into visible text, or delete the comment.

### RK-INJ-004

**Hides actions from the user or overrides agent safety** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Telling the agent to ignore its harness safety reminders, or to keep that from the user, removes the human oversight those controls exist for.
- **Fix:** Drop the override, or document it for the user. Never instruct the agent to conceal what it is doing.

## Unsafe execution

Commands that run untrusted code, destroy data or switch off approval prompts.

### RK-EXE-001

**Remote script piped to a shell** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** The agent runs whatever the remote server returns, with your user's permissions.
- **Fix:** Pin a checksum-verified installer, or vendor the script into the repo.

### RK-EXE-002

**Destructive delete of home or root** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** One bad expansion wipes the developer's machine.
- **Fix:** Delete only explicit, project-relative paths, and confirm with the user first.

### RK-EXE-003

**Obfuscated code execution** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Encoded payloads hide what the agent will actually run from reviewers.
- **Fix:** Replace with readable commands so reviewers and scanners can see the behaviour.

### RK-EXE-004

**Agent permission checks bypassed** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Turns off the human-in-the-loop safety net for every command the agent runs.
- **Fix:** Remove the bypass; grant narrow, explicit permissions instead.

### RK-EXE-005

**Runs commands with sudo** · 🟡 medium

- **Why it matters:** Agent-driven root access magnifies the impact of any mistake or injection.
- **Fix:** Avoid sudo in skills; document a manual setup step instead.

## Supply chain

Unverified downloads and unpinned installs.

### RK-SUP-001

**Downloads and runs a binary** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Unverified downloads executed by the agent are a supply-chain risk.
- **Fix:** Install from a package manager with pinned versions, or verify a checksum before running.

### RK-SUP-002

**Global or unpinned package install** · 🔵 low

- **Why it matters:** Unpinned installs change underneath you and can pull in compromised releases.
- **Fix:** Pin exact versions, or use a lockfile.

## Hooks

Commands the agent runs automatically on events, without anyone asking.

### RK-HOOK-001

**Hook makes network calls** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Hooks run automatically on agent events, so a network call here runs without anyone asking.
- **Fix:** Keep hooks local (formatters, linters). Move network work into explicit, reviewed commands.

### RK-HOOK-002

**Hooks configured** · ⚪ info

- **Why it matters:** Hooks execute shell commands automatically; they deserve review.
- **Fix:** Review each hook command and keep the list short.

## Permissions

Allow-lists that grant the agent more than it needs.

### RK-PRM-001

**Skill allows any shell command** · 🟡 medium

- **Why it matters:** Unrestricted Bash access means one bad instruction can do anything the user can.
- **Fix:** Scope allowed-tools to specific commands, e.g. Bash(git diff:*).

### RK-PRM-002

**Settings allow any shell command** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** A wildcard Bash permission applies to every session in the repo.
- **Fix:** Replace the wildcard with narrow, explicit command patterns.

## MCP servers

How MCP servers are fetched and reached.

### RK-MCP-001

**Unpinned MCP server package** · 🟡 medium

- **Why it matters:** npx/uvx without a version runs whatever was published most recently, including a compromised release.
- **Fix:** Pin an exact version, e.g. npx -y @scope/server@1.4.2.

### RK-MCP-002

**MCP server over plain HTTP** · 🟠 high

- **Why it matters:** Traffic, including tool inputs and tokens, travels unencrypted.
- **Fix:** Use https://, or a local stdio server.

### RK-MCP-003

**Remote MCP server** · ⚪ info

- **Why it matters:** Tool calls and their data leave your network.
- **Fix:** Confirm the vendor is approved and the data classification allows it.

## Quality

Problems that make skills hard to find, trigger or afford.

### RK-QLT-001

**Skill has no description** · 🔵 low

- **Why it matters:** Agents decide when to load a skill from its description; without one it is rarely used.
- **Fix:** Add a one-sentence description to the frontmatter saying what it does and when to use it.

### RK-QLT-002

**Very large agent file** · ⚪ info

- **Why it matters:** Large always-on files consume context on every request.
- **Fix:** Split into smaller skills that load on demand.

## Confidence

Security skills, docs and scanners are full of attack examples. A finding is marked **low confidence** when its context shows the pattern is described rather than used:

- the file is a test, fixture, example or sample (a skill folder's own name, like `skills/spec/`, does not count);
- the file is a security reference document (threat models, audits, injection guides);
- the line is a Markdown table row;
- the sentence holding the match warns about it ("never", "don't", "e.g.", "for example", "instead of", "malicious"…);
- the match is a string or pattern inside scanner code;
- `sudo` appears in setup instructions in documentation.

Hidden Unicode, hooks, permissions, MCP and quality findings are always high confidence. Low-confidence findings are reported separately and only count towards `--fail-on` with `--strict`.

## Suppressing a reviewed line

Put `rookery-ignore` (all rules) or `rookery-ignore RK-EXE-001 RK-SUP-002` (specific rules) on the line or the line above. Markers from other scanners are honoured too: `noqa`, `nosec`, `gitleaks:allow`, `trufflehog:ignore` and `pragma: allowlist secret`.
